column1: # findmypast, "Uruguay Baptisms 1750-1900", surname LERENA. 33 index rows; 20 distinct children.
# *** THE TRANSCRIPTS ARE OPEN, 27 September 2026. *** This file sat for eighteen days under a header
# that said "transcripts are behind findmypast's paywall and were NOT opened", carrying parents'
# FORENAMES ONLY and years without days. David signed in and all thirty-three opened. Every row below
# now has the MOTHER'S SURNAME and an EXACT BAPTISM DATE, which is the whole difference between a list
# of names and a set of families.
# *** THE DUPLICATE PAIRS ARE REAL AND ARE NOT ERRORS. *** Thirteen of the thirty-three are second
# copies of the same act under a different record id, agreeing in every field. They are listed once.
# *** WHAT IT CONFIRMED, AND THE ARCHIVE PREDICTED IT. *** /uruguay/ has said the Trinidad kindred
# married BASQUE women - "Beloqui, Echeverry, Pelaez". The transcripts give BELOQUI/BELOGIN,
# ECHEVERSE/ECHEVERSI/ECHEVERRY and PELAEZ, plus BARRAGAN and GAZO/GOSA. The prediction was made from
# three surnames in a dispensation; it holds across five households.
# *** AND THE SPELLING DRIFTS WITHIN ONE FAMILY. *** Andrea's surname is Echeverse in 1873, Echeversi
# in 1875 and Echeverry in 1877 - three spellings, one woman, one parish, four years. Adelaida is Gazo
# in 1874 and Gosa in 1875, and Gosso on an Argentine death record. Cipriano's wife is Lauriana Beloqui
# in 1876 and Laurena Belogin in 1877. *** THIS IS THE SEVEN-SPELLINGS PROBLEM ON THE MOTHERS' SIDE ***,
# and a search run under one of them misses the rest.
# *** FOUR HOUSEHOLDS HERE ARE NEW TO THIS ARCHIVE: *** Manuel x Juana FERREIROZ and Manuel x Dolores
# ESPINDOLA (two Manuels at Montevideo, or one with two wives - NOT established), Pedro A. x Manuela
# LEMOS, and Fermin x Paulina BARRAGAN. And THREE LERENA WOMEN appear as MOTHERS at San Jose - OLEGARIA,
# ESTEFANIA and FELICIA - which is a side of that cluster the archive has never counted.
# TIER: findmypast transcript of an IGI index entry. *** SECONDARY. *** It is an index of an index, and
# no image was opened here. The acts themselves are in the Uruguayan parish books and this file is a
# pointer to them, not a substitute - the rule this archive keeps having to relearn.
